title: Singing on the date: Romance Without Finance
summary: Grimes explains the vocal numbers, letting Parker play, and the one-mike conditions.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Did he tell you in advance that he wanted singing on the records?

That was at the date. He just asked me that, could I do any singin'... I think he probably meant blues, really. I wouldn't be surprised. I said yeah, but I sung that thing. Only thing was he put his name on there as the writer of the words... How much nerve can you have...
So you sang You'll always love me just the same and Romance without finance.

Yeah Romance without finance. That went over pretty good, better than the other one. But even so I let Parker play. I never held him back yet. We only had 4 sides, I let him play on every side that there was. I didn't hold him back at all.
Did you do a lot of takes or talk overs.
Did it take a longer time to get Romance together?

I had been doin' that at the club, but I mean at the recording session it was different came at that time they didn't have no stereo and 3 or 4 mikes. Everybody had to use one mike or maybe two. And there was no tracks... It was more or less
the volume 'cause we knew the song --- sometimes the engineer can't get his thing together.
